claims.text: The 'forest' is a product metaphor, not a claim that software is an acyclic tree.
claims.why: The docstring explicitly states this is a metaphor; no code contradicts it.

claims.text: A repository contains cycles, relations with different meanings, and groups that cannot be represented faithfully as pairwise edges.
claims.why: The module exposes a multiplex graph with explicit hyperedges (declared but not implemented yet) and has ForestEdge with directed flag and evidence tuple.

claims.text: This module therefore exposes a multiplex graph with explicit hyperedges
claims.why: Hyperedge data structure not present in this chunk; only simple edges exist.

claims.text: nodes are indexed source files, and -- when the index carries them -- DOCUMENTS and TYPES/FIELDS, which are the same contract with a different ``kind``
claims.why: No index or node kinds defined in this chunk; ForestNode has a 'kind' field but no enumeration.

claims.text: edge layers keep imports, document links, type structure and temporal co-change evidence separate
claims.why: No edge layers defined in this chunk; ForestEdge has 'relation' field but no layer abstraction.

claims.text: hyperedges preserve clone groups without expanding them into fake cliques

Symbols, build targets, schemas, runtime spans, and domain entities can be added as new node kinds and relation layers without changing this contract -- ``document`` (node kind) and ``documents`` (relation layer) were added exactly that way, and ``type``/``field`` were added the same way again, and all three cost this file no new field, no new dataclass and no schema bump.
claims.why: ForestNode and ForestEdge use generic 'kind' and 'relation' strings and 'attributes' mapping, allowing extensibility without schema change.

claims.text: No latent coordinates or partitions are inferred here. The snapshot is evidence-preserving input for later, independently evaluated algorithms.
claims.why: The dataclasses store data as provided; no inference logic present.

claims.text: NOT EVERY NODE KIND IS A FILE, AND THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT ... ``document`` joined ``dss.FILE_NODE_KINDS``; ``type`` and ``field`` deliberately did NOT, and a future reader must not "finish the job" by adding them.
claims.why: References to dss.FILE_NODE_KINDS not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A document has BYTES ON DISK. It can be a hierarchy leaf, a selection seed and a candidate for a token budget, because ``n_tokens`` is a measurement of it. A ``type`` node is a DERIVED assertion about a region of a file that is already a node in its own right; it has no bytes of its own. Pack it and ``dss._estimated_tokens`` falls through to its ``loc * 8`` fallback and invents a cost for something that cannot be read into a prompt -- the token accounting stops being accounting and becomes fiction, while the file that actually contains the declaration may be omitted for lack of budget. So a type node is EVIDENCE THAT RE-SCORES FILE NODES, never a packable item.
claims.why: References to dss._estimated_tokens and token budget logic not present.

claims.text: The same asymmetry holds for the safety fence. ``graph.fenced_dominance`` divides by ``graph._graph_nodes``, which is fed by ``index["modules"]`` and ``index["import_edges"]``. Type nodes have no forward imports, so every one of them would land in the denominator and none in the numerator: ``fraction`` falls, ``provider_router``'s reachability stand-down stops firing, and every task stays on the premium lane. That is real money spent for a wrong reason, which is why the type layer lives in ``type_nodes``/``type_edges`` and never in ``modules`` or ``import_edges``. This file honours that by keeping ``module_ids`` (the membership gate of four other layers) closed to them.
claims.why: References to graph, index, provider_router not present.

claims.text: And the type relations are a LENS, not a diffusion channel. The fan-in of ``Path``/``dict``/``str`` in this repo was MEASURED before the layer was built: uncapped, "two functions that mention the same type are two hops apart" makes 53.6% of all function pairs adjacent, i.e. the graph is effectively complete. So ``dss._relation_adjacencies`` filters diffusion to file-kind endpoints; these layers are published for consumers that ask about them by name, and the hub cap that would make them diffusible is measured and reported in ``index["types"]["coverage"]``, not assumed.
claims.why: References to dss._relation_adjacencies and index not present.
_json_value sorts dict keys and set items, converts Path to posix string, and handles primitive types deterministically.
